Scenario:
AITA for getting mad at my bf for always walking in front of me? | Everytime my boyfriend and I are walking somewhere, he tends to walk much faster than me. I’m actually a pretty fast walker myself when alone, but when going out with him, either I’m in heels half the time so it’s harder to walk super fast, or even in flats, sometimes I just want to walk alongside him and hold hands and have a conversation. It’s hard to hear him or I’m struggling to keep up. I’ve brought it up to him multiple times but he says he just has longer strides (he’s maybe 6” taller than me) and can’t help it. We just went on vacation and walking around a new city, it was the same thing and I finally blew up at him saying that I don’t feel like his girlfriend when he won’t ever walk beside me. AITA and he really can’t help it?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw:
0 (NTA - Not The Asshole)

I think it's reasonable for you to feel frustrated and want to walk alongside your boyfriend, holding hands and having a conversation. It's not about him intentionally trying to leave you behind, but rather a lack of awareness and consideration for your feelings and needs.

While it's true that he may have longer strides due to his height, it's not impossible for him to adjust his pace to match yours. It's a matter of being mindful and making an effort to walk together, rather than just assuming that you'll keep up.

By bringing it up multiple times and still not seeing any change, it's understandable that you felt the need to express your feelings and concerns. Your outburst may have been a culmination of built-up frustration, and it's possible that your boyfriend didn't realize the impact his behavior was having on you.

It's not about him being unable to help it, but rather about being willing to make an effort to accommodate your needs and desires. A simple solution could be for him to make a conscious effort to slow down, wait for you, or even just ask if you're comfortable with the pace. By doing so, he can show that he values your feelings and your relationship, and is willing to work together to find a compromise that works for both of you.
